sections.html:
Wilkinson County splits the work between two desks in Irwinton. The assessors put a value on each parcel. The tax commissioner mails the statement and takes the money. Georgia's rule on timing is simple: whoever holds title on January 1 owes the year's tax, and a spring closing earns no rebate from the county.

Context for pricing: the county had 8,877 residents in 2020 and an estimate of 8,650 for July 2025, down from 10,368 in 1980. Median home value runs $86,300, and owners live in 80.5% of houses. A buyer pool this small makes a clean tax record worth more than it would in a busy market.

Gather these before you talk to any buyer:

  • last year's bill and the newest assessment notice
  • a note of whether the parcel has a homestead exemption on file
  • the location permit and tax receipt for any manufactured home on the land
  • any letter from the commissioner about overdue balances

With those in hand, the title company can order a payoff figure and the closing stays on schedule.

Match the question to the desk and the visit goes quickly.

  • Tax Commissioner at 100 Bacon St., Suite 136, open 8:00 a.m. until 4:45 p.m. Phone (478) 946-2232, fax (478) 946-1429, postal box P.O. Box 182. Online payments add a convenience fee.
  • Board of Assessors and Chief Appraiser, P.O. Box 189, phone (478) 946-2076. This office keeps the tax maps, the ownership transfers, and the records for mobile homes without a homestead. It meets the first Wednesday of the month at 9:30 in the courthouse.
  • Board of Equalization, whose members the grand jury appoints. Each member completes 40 hours of training in the first year and eight hours yearly after that. The Clerk of Superior Court supplies clerical help only.
  • Commissioners and school board, the two bodies that set the rates.

The county website, wilkinsoncounty.net, links to a property record search and posts the current digest with a five-year levy history. Call the commissioner for anything about a bill and the assessors for anything about value.

Your rate depends on where the house sits, since a city levy stacks on top of the county, state and school pieces. These are the 2025 combined totals the assessors post.

Combined 2025 millage by jurisdiction
JurisdictionCombined millage
Unincorporated county32.082
Allentown37.082
Danville32.082

Irwinton37.892
Ivey37.47
McIntyre35.302

A mill is one dollar per thousand dollars of assessed value, and assessed value is 40% of fair market value. For 2024 the county government trimmed its own levy from 14.344 to 13.786 mills, still above the 13.227 rollback figure, which is why public hearings were required.

A house in Irwinton carries a higher combined rate than one in Danville or the unincorporated county, so a buyer comparing two listings should ask for the actual millage on each parcel.

December 20 is the usual deadline in Wilkinson County, and the date printed on your bill controls. Georgia lets a county substitute December 1, November 15, or several installments.

No interest accrues for the first 60 days after the postmark on your bill. Penalties may follow later, so get the office's current charges in writing along with your payoff.

  • Returns come in between New Year's Day and April 1.
  • A real property return renews itself at the previous value each year, so a new filing is needed only when you add structures or buy more land.
  • Ignored bills can lead to a levy against the parcel and a forced sale.

If you are selling in the fall, ask the commissioner whether the bill has been mailed yet. A closing that falls just before the due date is the easiest time to leave a balance behind, so settle it at the table.

An appeal goes to the assessors in writing, and the postmark has to land inside a 45-day span that opens when the notice is sent. You can dispute what the property is worth, how it compares with neighbors, whether it is taxable, or an exemption you were refused.

On the state form you name your forum: the equalization board, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. Revenue department staff have no power to overturn any of those rulings on one house.

A second entry point is the annual return. Declaring a different value on a return filed by April 1 opens an appeal if the assessors reject your figure.

Bring recent sales of similar houses nearby, photographs of defects, and contractor estimates. With homes valued at a median $86,300 here, a few thousand dollars of correction can matter, so documented condition problems are worth the effort.

The exemption trims the assessed value of the house you occupy as your main residence. The state default is $2,000, and a county may offer more through local legislation. In Wilkinson County the Chief Appraiser takes homestead applications.

File whenever you like. A form arriving after April 1 waits for next year, and an owner who never files is treated as having waived it.

A buyer needs a fresh application of their own after closing. If you moved out and rented the house, ask the Chief Appraiser how the parcel is classified before you list it.

sections.h2: Selling with back taxes or a lien
sections.html:
Your title company asks the commissioner for a payoff figure and deducts it from your proceeds. If a FiFa lien was filed, it appears on the Clerk of Superior Court's execution docket until the tax, fees and interest clear.

Write the proration into the contract, since the county bills one owner of record and never divides a year between two people.

Manufactured homes have extra steps. State guidance gives the owner 30 days after placement to obtain a location permit, then a yearly renewal each winter, plus a return due April 1. Check that all three are current before you advertise.

A cash buyer who purchases as-is can skip repair negotiations, but the tax payoff and any lien release still happen at closing exactly as they would in a listed sale.

Start by pulling your latest bill and assessment notice, then call the commissioner's office to ask whether anything is overdue. Next, confirm with the Chief Appraiser that your homestead filing is on record. Once you have a buyer, the title company requests the payoff and the contract sets how the year's tax is split between the two of you. After closing, the buyer files their own homestead application and you forward any stray mail about the parcel. If a manufactured home sits on the land, add the permit and renewal check to that list before the sale date, since the commissioner can refuse to issue paperwork while a balance is open.

faqs.q: Who mails the property tax statement in Wilkinson County?
faqs.a: The tax commissioner does. The office is on Bacon Street in Irwinton and answers at (478) 946-2232. Value disputes belong to the assessors at (478) 946-2076.

faqs.q: Is December 20 the due date for Wilkinson County taxes?
faqs.a: Usually, but follow the date on your own bill, because a county can pick an earlier deadline.

faqs.q: What is the window for contesting a Wilkinson County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, counted from the date the notice is sent. Address the written appeal to the assessors at P.O. Box 189.

faqs.q: Does a mid-year sale shift the tax to the buyer?
faqs.a: Not automatically. The owner on New Year's Day is responsible for the full year, so sellers and buyers usually divide the bill inside the contract.

faqs.q: Where is the homestead exemption filed in Wilkinson County?
faqs.a: At the assessors' office, where the Chief Appraiser takes applications.
